tldr: For two fixed-cohort binary risk differences under balanced complete randomization, the smallest warranted common Gaussian square radius is \(c^\star(p,u)\). A binary covariance-skeleton theorem and a singularity-safe directed evaluator give convergent radius certificates and complete limiting covers of every maximizing coupling fiber. For every equal-margin pair, including rank-one and zero covariances, the closed-form reduction is \(c^\star(p,u)=q(u,4S_1(p))\), with the diagonal coupling uniquely worst. Both original open-ended questions are discharged: the agreement/disagreement benchmark has one globally proved confidence switch, while the positive-cell family has complete endpoint classifications and an exact tie equation. Structural calibration results hold for \(u\in(0,1)\). Observed arm counts give uniform asymptotic simultaneous coverage on the maintained prevalence class for \(\alpha\in[1/100,1/2]\), and deterministic limiting common radii cannot be reduced. The undercoverage witnesses also yield the same comparison-class converse in any larger experiment class containing this balanced binary subclass.
